sights.n: Ōkurayama Ski Jump Stadium & Sapporo Olympic Museum (大倉山ジャンプ競技場)
sights.w: The 1972 Winter Olympics large hill — ride the chairlift to the top-of-jump observatory over the city, then the Olympic Museum at its foot.

sights.n: Shiroi Koibito Park (白い恋人パーク)
sights.w: Ishiya's Tudor-style chocolate factory behind Hokkaido's most famous souvenir cookie — factory line views, cookie workshops, a free courtyard and café.

sights.address: Minami 3-jō Higashi 1–2-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0053, Japan
sights.w: A city block of crab, uni, ikura and fish stalls since the Meiji era, with kaisendon counters and the Noren Yokochō drinking alley.

sights.address: Minami 4-jō – Minami 7-jō Nishi 2–6-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: Japan's biggest entertainment district north of Tokyo — the Nikka neon man, Ramen Yokochō, izakaya towers and the February ice-sculpture site.

sights.n: Sapporo Curb Market — Jōgai Shijō (札幌場外市場)
sights.address: Kita 11-jō Nishi 21–22-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0011, Japan
sights.w: Around 60 stalls and seafood diners on the edge of the Central Wholesale Market — early-morning crab and kaisendon away from the downtown crowds.

sights.n: Tanukikōji Shopping Street (狸小路商店街)
sights.address: Minami 2/3-jō Nishi 1–7-chōme, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido 060-0062, Japan
sights.w: Hokkaido's oldest shopping arcade (1873) — seven covered blocks of drugstores, souvenir shops, retro diners and the market at 7-chōme.
